limitations: Historical report extracts, not a live or comprehensive market feed. A source check does not discover newer reports.
All map polygons are hand-drawn navigation selectors, not reporting footprints or administrative boundaries.
Only City and West End have verified same-definition values in this snapshot; Canary Wharf and Midtown / Fringe remain missing.
Rent unit is GBP/sq ft as quoted. The articles do not explicitly state a billing period; no per-annum conversion is inferred.
Snapshot-calculated changes and publisher-reported growth are separate. Changed baselines or samples have not been established.
Report events are historical research commentary, not a live news service. No building-level market observations are provided.

evidence.quote: At the end of 2024, the average City prime rent stood at £98.60 per sq ft
The average Prime rent achieved across the West End at the end of the year stood at £157.50 per sq ft
In terms of Grade A rents, the average City rent stood at £70.51 per sq ft, which was up 2.8% on 2023; meanwhile, the West End average remained broadly stable, at £95.27 per sq ft.
The City market accounted for most of the fall in supply, with the City vacancy rate declining a further 90 bps to 7.9% during the quarter.
the average City Prime rent reached a new record high of £105.26 per sq ft, which was up 6.8% on the previous year.
The West End market also saw strong average prime rental growth over the year, with the average Prime rent standing at £166.61 per sq ft, up 6.1% year-on-year.

With the sustained preference for Grade A office space remaining, the average Grade A rent for the City at the end of the year stood at £74.34 per sq ft, which is up 4% on 2024, and the West End average Grade A rent stood at £99.58 per sq ft, up 5% on 2024.
Both the City and West End recorded a decline in supply over the quarter, with vacancy rates reaching 7.0% and 7.9%, respectively.
recently redeveloped or comprehensively refurbished office space accounted for 68% of space acquired during 2024
lettings in recently developed or comprehensively refurbished offices accounting for 77% of space acquired during 2025
Gibson Dunn’s pre-letting of the 9th–12th floors (153,116 sq ft), and FTI Consulting’s pre-let of the 1st–3rd (144,452 sq ft) at PNB’s 1 Exchange Square, EC2.
comprehensive refurbishments accounting for 65% of the number of schemes set for delivery over the next four years (51% by sq ft)

notes.title: Flight to newer and refurbished space
notes.summary: Savills reports that recently redeveloped or comprehensively refurbished offices accounted for 68% of Central London space acquired in 2024. Central London context, not a building or individual-submarket statistic.

notes.title: Preference for quality remains strong
notes.summary: Savills reports that lettings in recently developed or comprehensively refurbished offices accounted for 77% of Central London space acquired in 2025. This is historical Central London context, not a submarket-specific rate.

notes.title: City pre-lets at 1 Exchange Square
notes.summary: Savills highlights Q4 2025 pre-lets by Gibson Dunn and FTI Consulting at 1 Exchange Square. A dated report event, not a live transaction feed or a rent observation for the building.

notes.title: Refurbishments form a larger share of planned schemes
notes.summary: Savills reports that comprehensive refurbishments represent 65% of the number of Central London schemes set for delivery over the following four years (51% by area). Forward-looking report context, not an observed completed-supply metric.

records.label: Overall vacancy rate
records.definition: The named whole City / West End vacancy rates, Central London aggregate vacancy, absolute available area and independently defined availability rate are kept separate. 'Overall' is a review classification, not an article-defined detailed denominator. Reused quotes do not resolve total inventory, marketed-but-occupied space, under-offers, gross/net area or exact statistical boundaries. The 2024 West End 40 bps decrease is only a quarterly movement, not an absolute year-end rate. Missing means not evidenced by these authorized materials, not zero or proof the market has no such data.

evidence.quote: A total of 557,416 sq ft was acquired across Central London, down 35% month on month (MoM) but 10% above August 2025, with the City accounting for 67% of space acquired.

evidence.section: Central London Office Market Watch — August 2026 / ytd
evidence.quote: This takes year-to-date (YTD) take-up to 6.13 million sq ft, 2% ahead of the corresponding period last year, 8% above the five-year average, and broadly in line with the ten-year average.
